items.title: Extract Text and Tables from PDFs with Python (PDF to Excel for Beginners)
items.description:
Pull the text and tables out of any PDF with Python and pdfplumber, then save them to Excel with pandas, step by step for complete beginners. You'll read an invoice, grab the total, turn a PDF table into a spreadsheet, and process a whole folder of invoices into one summary file, plus the fixes for tables without lines and scanned PDFs. Every output on screen is the real result of the code shown.

Chapters
0:00 The result
0:34 The plan
0:49 Why copy and paste fails
1:08 Install pdfplumber
1:29 The practice files
1:45 Step 1: read the text
2:42 Step 2: find one value

3:48 Step 3: extract a table
4:35 Step 4: save it to Excel

Install
pip install pdfplumber pandas openpyxl

step1.py (read all the text)
import pdfplumber

with pdfplumber.open("invoice_1042.pdf") as pdf:
    print("Pages:", len(pdf.pages))
    page = pdf.pages[0]
    text = page.extract_text()
    print(text)

find_total.py (find one value)
import pdfplumber

with pdfplumber.open("invoice_1042.pdf") as pdf:
    text = pdf.pages[0].extract_text()

for line in text.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("Total:"):
        total = line.split(":")[1].strip()
        print("Found the total:", total)

to_excel.py (PDF table to Excel and CSV)
import pdfplumber
import pandas as pd

with pdfplumber.open("report.pdf") as pdf:
    table = pdf.pages[0].extract_table()

df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
print(df)
df.to_excel("sales.xlsx", index=False)
df.to_csv("sales.csv", index=False)
print("Saved sales.xlsx and sales.csv")

batch.py (a whole folder of invoices into one spreadsheet)
from pathlib import Path
import pdfplumber
import pandas as pd

rows = []
for path in sorted(Path("invoices").glob("*.pdf")):
    with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
        text = pdf.pages[0].extract_text()
    info = {"file": path.name}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        for label in ["Invoice number", "Date", "Customer", "Total"]:
            if line.startswith(label + ":"):
                info[label] = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
    rows.append(info)

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
df["Total"] = df["Total"].astype(float)
print(df)
print("Grand total:", df["Total"].sum())
df.to_excel("invoices_summary.xlsx", index=False)

Table without lines? Use the text strategy:
settings = {"vertical_strategy": "text", "horizontal_strategy": "text"}
table = page.extract_table(settings)

Common problems:
extract_table() returns None  -  the table has no drawn lines: use the text strategy above
extract_text() returns ''  -  it's a scanned PDF (only an image), you need OCR
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pdfplumber'  -  run python3 -m pip install pdfplumber
FileNotFoundError  -  check the exact file name and cd into the folder first
